target_customer: Itself and uranium offtakers: Terranox acquires mineral rights, explores and aims to sell discoveries or production rights to the nuclear fuel market in North America
problem: Uranium exploration relies on intuition, fragmented data and outsourced workflows. Terranox trains AI models on 70 plus years of exploration outcomes to find high-grade deposits.
business_model: Vertically integrated exploration company that uses AI for targeting and monetizes discoveries

founders.name: Jade Checlair
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. One profile lists her as CTO.

founders.name: Leeav Lipton
founders.background_notes: Astrophysics background per the YC page; degree not stated. A StartupHub write-up says the founders met in first-year physics and have collaborated for over 10 years.

competitors.name: KoBold Metals
competitors.what: AI driven mineral exploration focused on battery and critical minerals
competitors.traction_then: Zambian copper discovery reported by an aggregator
competitors.funding_then: Aggregator reports 537M USD Series C at 2.96B USD valuation in January 2025; unverified

competitors.name: Cameco, NexGen Energy, Denison Mines
competitors.what: Established uranium explorers and producers that run exploration in-house

technical_complexity.rationale: Physics informed models trained on decades of sparse geoscience outcomes plus field programs and mineral rights acquisition. Data is hard to assemble and ground truth arrives slowly.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary dataset and acquired claims could compound, but exploration success is uncertain and larger AI explorers like KoBold could target uranium.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found through 2026-11. One IsoEnergy announcement shows other uranium explorers deploying third party AI exploration tech.

market_need_then: Uranium demand rose with AI power demand and nuclear policy; one report puts spot at 85.75 USD per pound on 2026-06-22 after a 2026 high of 101.41 USD in January. Explorers need new high-grade deposits in North America.

branding.domain_note: Company uses terranox.ai, an exact match under .ai.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven, nuclear energy framing: find the fuel for the next century

branding.brand_signature: First AI-powered uranium discovery company claim

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive coined name that suggests earth, but no press about the brand itself; coverage is directory and launch pages.

outcome_analysis: Terranox is an active two person company in an unusually capital intensive niche. Founders pair geoscience and AI backgrounds and the uranium market has a policy and demand tailwind. No funding rounds are publicly verified, and discoveries will take years to confirm, so the outcome is open.
notes: The StartupHub write-up is an AI generated commentary; it claims 180K USD ARR within 11 days of launch, which is unverified and excluded. Some aggregators give conflicting founding year and location (2023, Vancouver); the YC page says 2025 and San Francisco. No funding, outcome, or name origin sources found. KoBold figures come from an aggregator and are unverified. Completeness pass: VCBacked (and Diffbot-sourced data) list a $500K pre-seed with no date; this is recorded as resting on a single database. StartupHub shows $1.5M raised, which conflicts and is not recorded. No press release found.
